# Capital Gains Calculator HQ

> Free capital gains tax calculator at capitalgainscalculatorhq.com with 2026 federal and state rates. Estimates short-term and long-term capital gains tax, the 3.8% NIIT, and state tax on stocks, crypto, or a home sale, including the home-sale exclusion. No sign-up, private, free.

Key facts:
- Uses 2026 federal brackets (0%/15%/20% long-term rates), the 3.8% net investment income tax, and every state's own treatment of capital gains.
- Compares short-term vs long-term outcomes and handles the primary-home-sale exclusion.
- All math runs in the browser; no financial data is uploaded or stored.

## Key numbers (2026, per IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32)

- Long-term capital gains breakpoints by taxable income: single 0% up to $49,450, 15% up to $545,500, 20% above; married filing jointly 0% up to $98,900, 15% up to $613,700, 20% above; head of household 0% up to $66,200, 15% up to $579,600, 20% above.
- Short-term gains are taxed as ordinary income (2026 federal brackets, 10% to 37%).
- Net investment income tax (NIIT): 3.8% on investment income above MAGI of $200,000 (single or head of household) or $250,000 (married filing jointly); statutory thresholds, not indexed.
- Home-sale exclusion (IRS Section 121): up to $250,000 of gain excluded ($500,000 married filing jointly) with the 2-of-5-year ownership and use tests.
- Washington: no income tax, but a 7% excise tax on long-term gains above roughly $278,000 (plus 2.9% above $1 million, 9.9% total); real estate exempt; short-term gains untaxed.
- Massachusetts: short-term capital gains taxed at 8.5%.
- Capital losses: offset gains dollar for dollar, then up to $3,000 per year against ordinary income; the remainder carries forward.
- State table source: Tax Foundation, State Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets (2026 edition).
